text: The season results stage is lit like a shop window, and {winner} steps into the glare alone.
{loser} reads the season sheet like a jeweller hunting for a scratch on the glass.
Every shelf on the results stage has been dusted, and {winner} is already waiting at the glass.
Engraved name plates line the back wall, and {loserClub} waits quietly for its name to be read.
Keys in hand, {winner} and the results board share a long, hushed moment before the figures go up.
Ribbons drape the lectern, silver sits on the sideboard, and {winnerClub} is polished for the night.
The results board glows at the far end of the stage while {loser} checks the cabinet glass once more.
A velvet-lined case waits by the results desk, empty for now, as {managerA} and {managerB} reach for the shelves.
Medals are laid out in a row across the stage, and the final figures are still hidden under a cloth.
The stage is set, every case lit, and {winnerClub} keeps its silver in the middle of the room.
Nobody needs an engraving tool tonight, only a steady hand on the results sheet and a cabinet about to fill.
{loserClub} sits beside a shelf of silver that looks heavier than it did before the reading began.
Before the season is read out, {winner} gives the trophy cabinet a final polish, more ritual than need.
The results stage is where the year's silverware gets counted, and {loser} arrives with a cloth and a steady gaze.
Lights rise over a row of glass cases and a sealed ledger, the season locked inside, waiting for the reading.
Keys jangle at the back of the hall as {managerA} unlocks the results room with {managerB} close behind.
That season's results sit on the lectern like the last piece on a shelf, and nobody has touched the glass yet.
Matching display cases stand side by side, and {managerA} and {managerB} look at them with the same level gaze.
The scales in the trophy room sit perfectly still, weighed down by equal silver on either side for {clubA} and {clubB}.
A matched pair of keys hangs on the same hook, and neither {managerA} nor {managerB} is ready to reach for it.
{clubA} and {clubB} have shelves that match in polish and shine, a stalemate of silver nobody wants to break.
Engraved plates sit in a neat line, and the names of {managerA} and {managerB} are cut at exactly the same depth.
The medals stop swinging together, and {managerA} and {managerB} exchange a nod across the glass.
A ribbon for {clubA}, a ribbon for {clubB}, both tied in the same knot and both waiting for a verdict.
{managerA} wipes the glass, {managerB} wipes the glass, and the reflections look like twins.
Dust settles evenly across both display cases, and neither {managerA} nor {managerB} has found a reason to claim the top shelf.
The ledger closes with the bottom line inked the same on both pages, {clubA} and {clubB} alike.
A stand-off in silver: {clubA} and {clubB} with cabinets of equal weight and polish, glowing in the spotlight.
The velvet is pressed flat on both shelves, marking the spot where a trophy would sit if the scoreboard tilted.
{managerB} hands over the cloth, {managerA} hands it straight back, and the cabinet keeps its shine a little longer.
Polish that cup until you can see your face in it, then go and find an empty shelf.
I will not sulk in the trophy room, {winner}, because the carpet deserves better.
Neither of us lifts it, so the room gets a fresh cloth and a shrug.
Honestly, the trophies do most of the talking. I just keep the ribbons straight.
Keep the key safe for me, {winner}, and do not let it get used as a bottle opener.
Nobody gets the glory from a draw, so the least we can do is split the dusting.
Engraving takes ages, so I told the engraver to leave room for my middle name.
Next season I will bring my own cloth, and the silver will know exactly who is coming.
A draw keeps the cabinet locked, and I have not decided whether to thank or blame the key.
Forget the medals, I am in it for the squeak the cabinet door makes when it opens.
Your display is gleaming, {winner}, and I am jealous in the most respectful way.
The lock sticks, so every time I open the doors I make a proper performance of it.
Nobody takes the big gold cup today, so we get to glare at it together, politely.
Engraved silver is lovely, but the best part is seeing my name spelled right for once.
I have dusted the ribbons again and again, which tells you exactly how I took the news.
A draw hands us the same view of the silver, and gloating is off the menu.
Trophies are only metal until somebody polishes them, so I keep a cloth in my pocket.
Well played, {winner}. Please tell the cabinet it can stop looking so smug about it.
A draw means the key stays in my pocket and yours, which is a very polite standoff.
The trophy room smells of polish and fresh victory, and I am glad to be its tenant.
Those medals look far too good on someone else, so I shall plan my revenge with a feather duster.
Every proud manager needs a locked door, a warm light and a rival who asks to see inside.
We both polish until the silver shows our faces, and nobody can say who looks better.
I have a shelf for every season, a drawer for the medals and a ribbon for the bad days.
Your name on that plate looks very grand, {winner}, so I will read it while I make tea.
A draw will not hand either of us a trophy, but it does hand us a duster and a grin.
Anyone can own a key, {loser}, but only a true champion remembers where the spare is.
My shelf has room for improvement, so I am spending the next few evenings with a saw.
No trophy moves tonight, so the room can finally have a sit down and so can we.
Gold in the case, silver in the drawer, and a grin so wide it needs its own shelf.

head: THE CONTINENT'S CROWN
text: {manager} has the continent's top prize under glass now, and {club} will polish it every morning.

head: TOP SHELF TENANT
text: The biggest trophy in the building has found its home, and {manager} has placed it on the top shelf with care.

head: THE UPPER CASE
text: {club} needed a bigger key for this prize, because the continental crown would not fit in any ordinary cupboard.

head: THE ENGRAVER'S BEST LETTERING
text: The engraver has been working through the night on the continental inscription, and {manager} wants every letter to shine.

head: CONTINENTAL MEDAL
text: {club} now hold the medal that matters most across the continent, and the ribbon has been pressed flat by a proud hand.

head: A FINER PLACE
text: Nobody on the continent has a finer place on the display than {manager}, whose crown now sits above every other silver piece.

head: KEY TO THE CASE
text: Hand over the key, {manager}, because the continental prize is ready for its spotlight, and the glass has never looked so bright.

head: SILVER FOR THE CONTINENT
text: {club} have carried the continent's top silver home, and the case is already too small for the kind of glory on show.

head: POLISH THE CROWN AGAIN
text: The crown needs a polish before the photographers arrive, so {manager} has gathered the cloths and started on the big gold piece.

head: THE RECORD BOOKS
text: Under the lights, {club} lifted the continent's most famous prize, and the history books will need a fresh page for {manager}.

head: THE CROWN COMES HOME
text: The continental crown has come home to {club}, and {manager} has given it the proudest spot on the sideboard, facing the door.

head: THE LOCK CLICKS SHUT
text: The lock clicks shut on the top case, and {manager} keeps the only key on a ribbon round the neck.

head: EUROPE'S PRIZE, ENGRAVED
text: A plate with the continent's name is being engraved right now, and {club} will have their own letters beside the glass soon.

head: HOME AT LAST
text: {manager} carried the grandest trophy in club football to the top of the stairs and set it down in the best case in the house.

head: CROWNED FOR THE CONTINENT
text: Few silver pieces on the continent shine like this, and {club} have bought the finest polish in town to keep it that way.

head: A NEW SHELF
text: The Europa silver has its own shelf, polished to a shine, and {manager} has promised it will never sit in the dark.

head: A BIGGER SMILE
text: It may not be the continent's top prize, but {club} have given it a glass case, a velvet cloth and a spot near the door.

head: THE OTHER CROWN
text: {manager} lifted the continent's other prize with the same care given to any silver in the room, and the ribbon looks finer for it.

head: A SMALLER PLATE, ENGRAVED
text: The engraver is cutting the name of {club} onto the modest plate, and the letters are so crisp they could slice glass.

head: WORTH THE POLISH
text: Every cloth in the house has been used on this prize, and {manager} still finds a fresh smudge to wipe away each evening.

head: THE SHELF FILLS UP
text: Once the shelf held nothing but dust, and now {club} have a European prize standing in front of the old silver with pride.

head: A KEY TURNS
text: {manager} turned the key on the European case with a flourish, then tucked the spare into a waistcoat pocket for safekeeping.

head: A NEW TENANT
text: A new tenant has moved into the glass case, and {manager} has promised the lodger a clean window, good light and steady polishing.

head: EARNS ITS PLACE
text: Some prizes take a long road to the shelf, and {club} earned this continental piece the hard way, through every round.

head: PROUDLY POLISHED
text: {club} have the polish out again, rubbing the continental prize until the engraving catches the light across the whole room.

head: A FINAL TOUCH
text: Before the case closes for the evening, {manager} adds a last touch of silver to the shelf, a small piece that has been waiting.

head: THE SIDE SHELF GLOWS
text: On the side shelf, {club} have a European prize glowing under the lamp, and visitors are asked to admire it without fingerprints.

head: THE LEAGUE'S PRIZE
text: The title has been wrapped in tissue and placed in the cabinet, where {manager} can admire its tarnish-free shine every morning.

head: A LEAGUE SHIELD
text: {club} have a league shield with fresh engraving, and the lettering is sharp enough to read from the far end of the shelf.

head: TITLE AT THE CENTRE
text: The league crown sits in the centre of the cabinet now, and {manager} has rubbed it until the reflection is just right.

head: POLISH WATCH
text: Cloths sharpened, elbows greased, the cups look nervous

head: KEYS INSIDE
text: The cabinet key turns at last, gently

head: SILVER SPECIAL
text: Hours of buffing for a shine too bright

head: ENGRAVED DAILY
text: Every nameplate read aloud, then read again

head: MEDAL DESK
text: Ribbons pressed flat, medals hung with pride

head: SHELF SPACE
text: Shelves measured, and the plan is bold

head: ARCHIVE FIND
text: Old ribbons unearthed in a dusty drawer

head: BRASS NOTICE
text: Brass plates buffed for the grand reopening

head: KEY HOLDERS
text: Only the caretaker holds the spare key

head: TROPHY ROOM
text: Velvet cloth and a steady hand, always

head: PLAQUE PRESS
text: Each plaque checked for spelling and pride

head: GLASS CASE
text: The glass case wiped down for guests

head: INSIDE JOB
text: Somebody polished the shelves all night long

head: SHINE ALERT
text: Gold leaf catching the lamps again

head: CABINET CALL
text: Doors open, silver out, inspection begins

head: RIBBON WATCH
text: Ribbons tied tight, bows straightened for the cameras

head: SILVER LINING
text: Silver on every shelf, no exceptions allowed

head: TOP SHELF
text: The best sits on the top shelf

head: MEDAL RUN
text: Medals sorted by weight, then by mood

head: LOCKED AWAY
text: Some trophies stay behind the glass for good

head: ENGRAVING NOW
text: Names carved into the base tonight

head: DUSTED OFF
text: Yesterday's dust has been politely removed

head: SHELF LIFE
text: The medals are living their best life

head: GLEAM WATCH
text: All cups in the room now gleam

head: KEEPER OF KEYS
text: The keeper of the keys keeps a list

head: NOTICE BOARD
text: Pinned to the door: handle with care

head: CASE CLOSED
text: Silver lined up, every label in place

head: SPARKLE INDEX
text: Brightness rated, sheen index updated

head: PALACE GRADE
text: Palace-grade polish applied with patience

head: HALL OF FAME
text: Names still climbing the wall of honour
